question: What is a formal business according to URA and why should informal businesses formalize?
answer: A formal business is an enterprise that is legally registered with the Uganda Registration Services Bureau (URSB) for a business or company name, registered for taxes with URA with an active Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN), and licensed to trade by the local municipal authority (such as KCCA or a local council). Formalization transitions businesses from vulnerability to legal recognition, brand protection, commercial credibility, and sustainable growth.

question: What are the three core steps to formalize a business in Uganda?
answer: Under the URA Business Formalisation Guide at https://ura.go.ug/en/business-formalisation/: 1) Step 1 — Business/Company Registration with URSB: Conduct a name search, reserve the business name, submit registration documents (Form S18, Memorandum & Articles of Association, Form A1 for companies), pay registration fees and stamp duty, and obtain a Certificate of Registration (sole proprietorships/partnerships) or Certificate of Incorporation (companies); 2) Step 2 — Tax Registration with URA: Apply online at https://ura.go.ug for an instant individual TIN (using NIN) or non-individual TIN (using URSB documents and director TINs); 3) Step 3 — Trading License Application: Obtain a trading license from KCCA or the local municipal council authorizing trade in that locality, renewable annually.

question: What are the 13 major commercial benefits of formalizing a business in Uganda?
answer: Under URA guidelines: 1) Competitiveness: Ability to bid for public and corporate tenders and engage in cross-border import/export trade; 2) Business growth & continuity: Enhanced brand reputation attracting broader clientele; 3) Access to investment incentives: Eligibility for government investment licenses and tax holidays; 4) Brand protection: Legal exclusivity over your business name; 5) Identity and pride: Official sense of business ownership; 6) Limited liability: Company debts are separated from personal assets; 7) Tax Clearance Certificates (TCC): Unhindered issuance of TCCs for licensing and regulatory approvals; 8) Banking & financial access: Eligibility for commercial bank loans and credit facilities above UGX 50M; 9) Credibility: High trust among suppliers and corporate clients; 10) Investor partnerships: Ease of attracting equity investors; 11) Land and motor vehicle transfers: Quoting TIN to process property transactions above UGX 10M; 12) Tax refunds: Legal right to claim overpaid tax refunds; 13) Authorized trading: Legal protection against local council closures.

question: How do I activate and log into a newly created URA web portal account after business registration?
answer: To activate your account: 1) Visit https://ura.go.ug; 2) Click 'Login' on the top right-hand corner; 3) Enter your 10-digit TIN as Login ID and the default password sent to your registered email during registration; 4) Promptly set a new secure password containing uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and special symbols (e.g. January@2030); 5) Return to the login page, enter your TIN, new password, and captcha to access your e-Tax self-service portal.

question: What ongoing tax obligations must a newly formalized business comply with?
answer: After formalization, a business must: 1) Timely file statutory tax returns via portal.ura.go.ug (provisional and final income tax, monthly VAT by 15th, monthly PAYE by 15th); 2) Make timely payments by return due dates via PRN; 3) Issue fiscalized e-invoices/e-receipts through EFRIS if VAT-registered; 4) Keep accurate business transaction records in English for at least five (5) years under Section 15 TPCA.

question: Where can I download the official URA Business Formalisation Guide?
answer: The official booklet 'FORMALISING A BUSINESS' (Vol. 1 Issue 2 FY 2024-25, 8 pages) is downloadable at https://ura.go.ug/storage/2024/01/BUSINESS-FORMALISATION-ENGLISH-FY-2024-25.pdf and published under Tax Education at https://ura.go.ug/en/business-formalisation/.
